learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how atoms combine to build the universe! Understand valency, how to write chemical formulas, and the difference between isotopes and isobars.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A molecule is formed when two or more atoms chemically bond together (like $O_2$). A compound is a specific type of molecule made of two or more DIFFERENT elements (like $H_2O$).
Electrons fill shells starting from the inside out: K shell (holds 2), L shell (holds 8), M shell (holds 18). The electrons in the very outermost shell are called 'valence electrons'.

Atoms want to be stable, which usually means having 8 electrons in their outer shell. 'Valency' is the number of electrons an atom needs to gain, lose, or share to reach this stable state. This determines how it bonds!
When an atom loses an electron, it becomes a positive ion (Cation). When it gains an electron, it becomes a negative ion (Anion). Opposites attract, creating strong ionic bonds (like salt, $NaCl$).

Isotopes are atoms of the SAME element (same protons) but with a different number of NEUTRONS (different mass), like Carbon-12 and Carbon-14. Isobars are atoms of DIFFERENT elements that happen to have the same mass number.

fun_activity.title: 🤝 The Valency Handshake
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine Oxygen has 6 valence electrons and wants 8 to be happy. It has 2 'empty hands' looking for a handshake. Hydrogen has 1 electron and 1 'hand'. Oxygen needs TWO Hydrogens to hold both hands. Boom! You just built $H_2O$!

exam_tips: 📌 Practice writing chemical formulas using the 'criss-cross' valency method. (e.g., Magnesium has valency 2, Chloride is 1 -> $MgCl_2$).
📌 Be able to draw the Bohr model (circles with dots) for the first 20 elements. Oxygen (atomic number 8) is drawn as 2, 6.
📌 Know the applications of isotopes: Uranium-235 for carbon dating, Cobalt-60 for cancer treatment, Iodine-131 for medical imaging.
quick_recap: ⭐ The chemical properties of an element depend entirely on its valence electrons.
⭐ Noble gases (like Neon and Argon) have naturally full outer shells, so their valency is 0. They are unreactive.
⭐ Fractional atomic masses exist because they are the weighted average of all an element's natural isotopes.
